newsitem.title: UK: Euro to aid market transparency, globalisation - BOE.
newsitem.headline: Euro to aid market transparency, globalisation - BOE.

text.p: The introduction of the single currency will aid the globalisation and transparency of markets, Bank of England executive director Ian Plenderleith told a trade magazine on Wednesday.
"The planned introduction of the euro will further add to the process of globalisation and transparency of markets," he told the latest Euroweek.

"But while individual issuers' responses to the introduction of the euro will differ, the central challenge of benchmark issuance will remain the same - to strengthen investor confidence in bonds' long-term performance."
Last year Britain launched a $2.0 billion five-year FRN and a $2.0 billion five-year bond.
Plenderleith said the most striking change in the markets had been the ever-increasing globalisation.

"This has been seen in all aspects of the markets: the internationalisation of investors' portfolios, the currencies of issuance, the scope of investment banks' sales and trading networks, and the international variety of borrowers themselves," he said.
Added to this he said the transparency of pricing had been a "very healthy development".
Last June the BOE said it would be ready to provide access to Euro-denominated settlement accounts by 1999 regardless of whether Britain joined European monetary union then or not.
